diagnosis.what_happened: The compiler script compile_gold_standard_chapter4.py appended new sections onto a loaded base document (Chapter_4_Preamble_Source.docx) without checking, modifying, or replacing the preamble paragraphs. As a result, the compiled DOCX retained a stale preamble with disconnected glyphs, despite the markdown being correctly updated.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: By treating the base document as immutable and ignoring the preamble in the markdown truth, the compilation process introduced a sync drift, preserving a defect in the final DOCX.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: The compiler must dynamically inject the canonical preamble by parsing the introductory paragraphs from the markdown truth and clearing the stale preamble from the base document before appending.
diagnosis.rationale_why: To maintain 100% sync between the .md and .docx artifacts (Triad Artifact Invariant), the DOCX compilation must reflect all canonical content from the markdown, including headings and preambles.

desired_behavior: Compiler scripts must parse the markdown preamble and dynamically inject it into the base DOCX (or replace the stale paragraphs in the base DOCX) to ensure perfect synchronization between the markdown source of truth and the compiled DOCX output.
generalization: Never use an immutable base document that overrides the canonical markdown text. Build pipelines must always sync preambles and headings from the markdown source into the DOCX deliverable.

evidence.observed_value: Stale preamble retained in compiled DOCX
evidence.threshold_value: 100% synchronization of preamble between MD and DOCX
